question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{6X}{X-2}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{x(x-2)}{36},\,3\le x\le 6.
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\frac{6x}{x-2}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{6X}{X-2}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{6}\frac{6x}{x-2}\cdot \frac{x(x-2)}{36}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{3}^{6}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{3}^{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[216-27] \\  & =\frac{21}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
